Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

strike verb

hit

also knock, hit, beat

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: ad pulsandōs verberandōsque hominēs (Lewis & Short)

pulsō, pulsāre

verb, first conjugation

strike, knock

Of knocking at a door (ōstium pulsāre) and of hitting people.

Examples

  • ut Cratēs, cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit

    as Crates, when he saw an ignorant boy, struck the boy’s tutorQuint. 1.9.5

  • Nōlī frātrem pulsāre!

    Don’t hit your brother!composed

Other words

  • feriō, ferīre — strike, hit (with a blow)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 2.8.13: pugnō ferīre vel calce (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.1.36: sublīmī feriam sīdera vertice

    No perfect: percussī serves (Lewis & Short, after Varro).

  • percutiō, percutere, percussī, percussum — strike, hit

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 1.9.5: paedagōgum ejus percussit; Cic. de Or. 2.279: cum Catō percussus esset ab eō, quī arcam ferēbat (Lewis & Short)

  • verberō, verberāre, verberāvī, verberātum — beat, thrash

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 562: nōn puduisse verberāre hominem senem

See also hammer, hit.

SourcesLewis & Short: pulso

Lewis & Short: ferio · Lewis & Short: percutio · Lewis & Short: verbero
